chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kathīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Indeed, the first successor upon the face of the earth was Hibat Allah ibn Adam, and there was no Prophet who passed except that he had a successor. The totality of the Prophets were one hundred and twenty thousand Prophets, and among them were five Possessors of Resolve: Nūḥ, Ibrāhīm, Mūsā, ʿĪsā, and Muḥammad عليهم السلام. And indeed, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib was the Hibat Allah for Muḥammad, and he inherited the knowledge of the successors and the knowledge of those who were before him.”

Indeed, Muḥammad inherited the knowledge of those before him from among the Prophets and the Messengers. Upon the pillar of the Throne it is written: ‘Ḥamza is the Lion of Allah and the Lion of His Messenger and the chief of the martyrs,’ and in the crest of the Throne: ‘ʿAlī is the Commander of the Faithful.’

So this is our proof against the one who denies our right and rejects our inheritance. And nothing has prevented us from speaking while certainty is before us; so what proof could be more eloquent than this?”

key_terms.أُولُو الْعَزْمِ: the five prophets of highest resolve and rank
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: the Throne, indicating exalted heavenly inscription and divine authority
key_terms.حُجَّتُنَا: our proof, meaning decisive evidence for their right
key_terms.عِلْمَ: knowledge, especially the inherited sacred knowledge of prophets and successors
key_terms.مِيرَاثَنَا: our inheritance, referring to the inherited knowledge and authority of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.هِبَةُ اللَّهِ: the gift of Allah; here used as a title of honored succession
key_terms.وَرِثَ: inherited, meaning received divinely transmitted knowledge and authority
key_terms.وَصِيٍّ: a designated successor appointed after a prophet

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the inheritance of knowledge and succession from the prophets to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the continuity of divinely appointed successors from the earliest prophets and places Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام within that sacred line of inheritance. It emphasizes that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and his successors inherit divine knowledge, and it frames the rights and authority of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام as established by heavenly proof.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdul Rahman Bin Kaseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The first successoras upon the face of the earth was Hibtullah Bin Adamas, and there is none from a Prophetas of the past except that for himas was a successoras, and the entirety of the Prophets were one hundred and twenty thousand Prophets. From themas, five were Determined Ones (Ul Al-Azam) – Noahas, and Ibrahimas, and Musaas, and Isaas and Muhammadsaww, and that Aliasws Bin Abu Talibasws was the Hibtullahas of Muhammadsaww, and an inheritor of the Knowledge of the successorsas, and the knowledge of the ones who were before himas’.

As for Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, he<sup>saww</sup> inherited the knowledge of the ones<sup>as</sup> who were before him<sup>saww</sup> from the Prophets<sup>as</sup> and the Rasools<sup>as</sup>. It is inscribed upon the Register of the Throne: “Hamza<sup>as</sup> is a lion of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and a lion of His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>as</sup> and the chief of the martyrs”; and in the central facet of the Throne: “Ali<sup>asws</sup> Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>”.

So these are our<sup>asws</sup> proofs upon the ones who deny our<sup>asws</sup> rights and fight against our<sup>asws</sup> inheritances. And what prevents us<sup>asws</sup> from the speaking and in front of us<sup>asws</sup> is the conviction? So which proof can happen to be more eloquent than this?’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘The first successor and executor of the will on earth was Hibbatullah, the son of Adam. No prophet has ever left this world without first leaving behind one who would execute his will. The prophets were one hundred twenty thousand persons. Five of them were commissioned Messengers, like Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and Muhammad (s.a.) Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) was the Hibbatullah for Muhammad (s.a.).He inherited the knowledge of the executors of the wills of the prophets and the knowledge of those who were before him.

(Is not it true) that Muhammad (s.a.) inherited the knowledge of the prophets and the Messengers who lived before him? It is written on the columns of the throne, “Hamza is the loin of Allah and the loin of His Messenger. He (Hamza) is the master of the martyrs. On top of the throne is Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.).

This evidence against those who deny our rights and refuse to yield to us our right of inheritance. We are not forbidden to speak. Before us is all certainty. What supporting evidence could be more clear than this.”
